findings.title: T12/T13 guard `save_review_file`, but the `sq review code` path the success criterion names goes through `save_review_result`, which bypasses it
findings.description: The design's success criterion is "Re-running `sq review code <N>` over an edited review file archives the prior content and warns; nothing is silently destroyed" (walkthrough step 7 exercises exactly this: hand-edit the file, run `sq review code 305`, expect WARNING + `archive/` copy). I verified the code path: the CLI's `review code` command saves via `save_review_result` (`src/squadron/cli/commands/review.py:746`), and `save_review_result` writes the file directly with `path.write_text(...)` in both its markdown and JSON branches — it never calls `save_review_file`. T12 places the archive-on-overwrite guard only "before `save_review_file` writes to an existing `path`", and T13's tests exercise `save_review_file` directly. A junior completing T12/T13 to green leaves the actual data-loss path (CLI `sq review code`, and the pipeline's `slice_info` branch, which also uses `save_review_result`) silently overwriting hand-edited reviews — the exact bug Part D exists to fix. The task must either guard both write sites (e.g., extract a shared archive-then-write helper used by both, or route `save_review_result` through `save_review_file`) and T13 must include a test that reproduces walkthrough step 7 through `save_review_result`.

findings.title: T6's "no test may need rewriting" gate is unsatisfiable: moving the transport call site orphans 305's `_JUDGE_TRANSPORT` patch targets
findings.description: T5 moves the `run_review_with_profile` call into the new `review/addressed/judge.py` (`judge_residue_core`), where the name is resolved in that module's namespace. But both 305 suites patch the old module's attribute: `_JUDGE_TRANSPORT = "squadron.pipeline.actions.findings_addressed.judge.run_review_with_profile"` at `tests/pipeline/test_findings_addressed_judge.py:32` and `tests/pipeline/test_findings_addressed_e2e.py:27`. After the move, that patch either raises AttributeError (if the pipeline module drops the now-unused import) or silently fails to intercept (if it keeps the import), so the mock is never called and the real transport is hit — T6's required "all pass unchanged" cannot hold. T6 further instructs "if one did [need rewriting], the extraction changed behavior — stop and reconcile", which converts a one-line, behavior-preserving patch-target update (two string constants) into an unplanned halt. Fix: T5 should explicitly include updating the two `_JUDGE_TRANSPORT` strings to `squadron.review.addressed.judge.run_review_with_profile` as part of the relocation, and T6's criterion should be "same test count and assertions pass; only the patch-target strings changed" (the mock still intercepts the same call, so the proof of preserved behavior stands). Note the `no_transport` fixture in `test_findings_addressed.py` patches the source module `squadron.review.review_client` and is ineffective both before and after the move (screens never touch the transport) — it needs no change, so a junior should not be led into "fixing" it.

findings.title: T11 integration-covers only one of the two persistence paths the criterion requires
findings.description: The design criterion says `reviewedSha:` must be present "from both the CLI and the pipeline persistence paths". T10 correctly wires both (`save_review_result` and `pipeline/actions/review.py`), but T11's integration test is explicitly singular: "on `save_review_result` (or the pipeline review action, whichever is more directly testable)". If the junior picks the CLI path, the pipeline action's stamping — including its two-branch persistence (the `save_review_file` fallback branch, where the stamp must be threaded through the `format_review_markdown` call) — ships with no test, and the unit tests in T11 only cover the formatter. The file-2 walkthrough (T40 step 1) verifies only the CLI path end-to-end. T11 should require a test per path (a `ReviewAction`-level test or equivalent for the pipeline branch), mirroring the interface-parity rule the task itself cites.

findings.title: T8's baseline phrasing is muddled at T8's position in the plan
findings.description: T8 (which runs before any test-adding task — T11 and all of file 2 follow) expects "the same pass count as slice 305's close-out baseline (2832 passed, 2 skipped) plus this slice's later additions". At T8's point in time the relocation adds zero tests, so the expected count is exactly the pre-slice baseline; the "plus later additions" qualifier only makes sense when the full suite is re-run at file-2 closeout. The hard-coded 2832 figure is also unverifiable from here — T2's "same count as before the move" instruction (run the suite pre-change) is the reliable baseline mechanism, and T8 should lean on that comparison rather than the number.

findings.title: T1's expected-importer list names a test file with no code import of the package
findings.description: T1 lists "the four `tests/pipeline/test_findings_addressed*.py` files" as expected importers of `findings_addressed.models`. I verified `test_findings_addressed_e2e.py` has no code import of the package — only the string patch target at line 27 (which is the subject of the T5/T6 finding above). The task's grep is the authoritative mechanism, but a junior told to update importers may find nothing to change in that file and second-guess the list. The importer list should read "the test files that import from the package (per grep)".
